claim-EZ.note: Only E Z≤4G/m is stated, derived from the coefficient-two finite-world induction. The canonical row also asserts early and late subclaims, which are absent.

def-heavy.note: The predicate requires more than L target-address queries in the complete path; aQueries uses list countP and hence charges repeats.

def-simulator.note: The simTree definition reads target queries up to L, answers other queries from outside data, stops before the proposed query and returns its cell address or the all-false default. Its index t is zero-based, corresponding to the paper’s t+1.

def-deg.note: The type characterizes degree through Fourier support; it does not alone assert the row’s unique multilinear polynomial, constant-zero convention and input/output sign equivalences. Adjacent degree_const and degree_eq_sign are distinct declarations.

def-bs.note: The type fixes the supremum over inputs and families. The nonempty block and flipping semantics are separately given by appendixA_isSensitiveBlock_iff and the imported family definition.

def-Gamma-i.note: It states the entry mask exactly; the row also specifies the Euclidean operator-norm convention, a separate definition appendixAMatrixNorm.

premises: Γ real, symmetric and entrywise nonnegative.
claim-perron.note: AppendixAPerronWitness expands to coordinatewise nonnegative v, sum v²=1, and Γv=‖Γ‖v, with the Euclidean operator norm. Γ need not be nonzero; the input cube is nonempty even for n=0.

premises: Finite workspace W; arbitrary input-indexed state family Ψ.
def-adv-progress.note: Its body is the complex weighted sum vₓvᵧΓₓᵧ⟨Ψₓ,Ψᵧ⟩; substitution of the purified run at time t gives the paper definition. No absolute overlap replaces the inner product.

claim-restrict-parity.note: The same degree-sized face works for every outside assignment; its parity coefficient is nonzero and some parity agreement fiber has more than half the cube and sensitive edges. This is stronger than choosing one outside restriction.

def-huang.note: The definition recursively extends the signed block matrix to d=0. The explicit one-dimensional base and equality of its entrywise absolute value with cube adjacency are separate theorems, so this definition alone is partial for the compound row.

claim-huang-spectrum.note: Both half-dimensions are present for d>0. Square, trace and eigenvalue classification are separate declarations; this one remains partial against the compound corrected row.

claim-interlace.note: Its type gives a nonzero positive-root eigenvector supported on U and the unsigned induced Rayleigh inequality. The eigenspace dimension is proved using parity involution rather than the paper’s trace argument.

claim-round-block.note: It provides one degree-sized support containing a nonempty sensitive block at every input. The paper row also asserts the nonconstant restriction and disjointness of blocks over successive rounds; restriction transport and round accounting are separate declarations.
